title: Word Frequency and Top-K
hints: `word_counts` is one line per word: `++counts[w];`. On a key it has never seen, `std::map::operator[]` inserts the key with a value-initialized `int` (that is `0`), then returns a reference to it, so `++` turns it into `1`.

A `std::map` is always sorted by key, so you cannot sort it by count. Copy it into a `std::vector<std::pair<std::string, int>>` (the vector's range constructor accepts `counts.begin(), counts.end()`), `std::sort` that with a lambda comparator, then `v.resize(std::min(k, v.size()))` to keep the top `k`.
